subject: Citric acid
hook: CITRIC ACID IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK
angle: More than half of the citric acid we use today is not squeezed from lemons but is fermented by mold in factories, with over 50% of the 2 million‑ton annual production coming from China.
angle_support: More than two million tons of citric acid are manufactured every year.

Although industrial-scale production of citric acid by chemical synthesis or extraction from citrus fruits are both feasible, fermentation by molds (and sometimes yeasts) is almost exclusively the only method actually practiced.
Global production was in excess of 2,000,000 tons in 2018. More than 50% of this volume was produced in China.
title: The surprising source behind most citric acid
description: Most people think citric acid comes from lemons, but the majority is actually made by mold fermentation in factories, with China producing over half of the global supply. This explains why your soda’s sour punch isn’t lemon‑derived.
narration: CITRIC ACID IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK You picture citric acid being squeezed from lemons. In reality, over half of the two‑million‑ton annual output today is brewed by Aspergillus niger mold in factories, especially in China worldwide. More than two million tons of citric acid are produced annually. Fermentation with Aspergillus niger supplies virtually all of it, and over half of that output originates in China, making mold‑based synthesis the dominant source today for food and drinks. Mold, not lemons, fuels the citric acid in your soda every day worldwide
